react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolites converge on a coordinated response centred on cysteine bioavailability and xenobiotic metabolism. L-cysteine (C00097, InChIKey: XUJNEKJLAYXESH) is the dominant driver: it achieves enrichment across all three independent paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR=0.0019, Biological oxidations, REACT:R-HSA-211859), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p=0.013, Thiamine metabolism, hsa00730; p=0.015, Cysteine and methionine metabolism, hsa00430), and Mummichog m/z-direct (p=0.0034, Xenobiotics metabolism, MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism). The PAH metabolites Benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (C14853) and N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl (C20319) are Phase I cytochrome-P450 substrates that are metabolised by CYP1A1/CYP1A2 enzymes; these same enzymes are induced by electrophilic xenobiotics via the Nrf2-ARE pathway, which also up-regulates glutamate-cysteine ligase (GCLC) to increase glutathione synthesis from L-cysteine. Coumarin (C05851) is a canonical CYP2A6 substrate and co-occurs with these Phase-I enzymes in the xenobiotics metabolism module detected by Mummichog. Methimazole (C07190) is a thionamide that depletes ROS via direct scavenging and by disrupting thyroid peroxidase-mediated H2O2 generation, while beta-mercaptoethanol (C00928) is a low-molecular-weight thiol that augments the cellular reducing environment. The convergence across ORA (RaMP, MetaboAnalystR) and m/z-direct (Mummichog) paradigms on cysteine-linked pathways and xenobiotic metabolism defines the biological signature: a treatment-induced shift toward Phase I/II detoxification and electrophilic stress defence, with enhanced cysteine flux into glutathione synthesis as the central metabolic hub.

RaMP multi-database ORA identifies Biological oxidations (REACT:R-HSA-211859) as the top hit, driven by L-cysteine and coumarin, with an FDR of 0.00186 and raw p-value of 0.000109 (fold enrichment 110.2). The Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently recovers Xenobiotics metabolism (MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism) as its top-ranked pathway, again with coumarin as the sole annotated input compound, at p=0.00387. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA anchors the cysteine signal through Cysteine and methionine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00730, p=0.0131) and Taurine and hypotaurine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00430, p=0.015), both using L-cysteine (KEGG:C00097, InChIKey XUJNEKJLAYXESH) as the single set member. Beta-mercaptoethanol and pyrocatechol appear in the input list but resolve to general or annotation-sparse entries in the compound networks, and are not recovered as driver hits.
